ref: Слово 2-е (Догматико-полемические сочинения, гл. 7 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910, с. 38–82): раздел о кончине века, близко к концу сочинения
quote_orig: Но, оставив подробно оплакивать наши злоключения, возвратимся к предлежащему и поймем из других божественных неложных изречений, что устроение всех, то есть, ожидаемая кончина века сего, не далеко отстоит, но находится близко, и что скверный Магомет есть самый упоминаемый в божественном Апокалипсисе лживый пророк и предтеча богоборного антихриста.
own_translation_en: But, leaving aside at length our lamentation over misfortunes, let us return to the matter at hand and learn from other divine, unerring sayings that the 'establishment of all' (устроение всех), that is the expected end of this age, is not far off but near, and that the wicked Muhammad is the false prophet most often mentioned in the divine Apocalypse and the forerunner of the God-fighting Antichrist.
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
licence_note: azbyka.ru (1910 printing, no licence statement seen): public domain by age, team to confirm. Russian translation, not a Slavonic/Greek original.
keys: самый упоминаемый в божественном Апокалипсисе лживый пророк
what_it_says: Muhammad is the 'false prophet' of Revelation and the forerunner of Antichrist, and the end of the age is near.
context: From the second discourse, addressed to the pious Orthodox. Maxim is explaining why the end of the age is near: the loss of Constantinople and of the Christian East is read as a sign, and he relies on Scripture (2 Thess. 2:3–4, Ps. 72, Rev.) to identify Muhammad with the false prophet.
limits: Maxim's own reading of Revelation and 2 Thessalonians, not a quotation of a source. The Russian text is a 1910 translation. Muhammad is not named as Antichrist; he is the 'forerunner'. The sentence itself contains the adjective 'скверный' (wicked). Famous status: UNVERIFIED.
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
cross_check: Second witness k-istine.ru (cp1251 page, older orthography, 'богоборнаго'): same sentence present with spelling variant. paraklit.org: same sentence, 'богоборного' absent (spelling variant 'богоборн-'). Status: VERIFIED in 2 of 3 copies (spelling variants); exact spelling of the 1910 text only in azbyka.ru.

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): рассказ о учителях Магомета (иудей и инок-арианин)
quote_orig: Всему этому научил его иудеянин, – чего раньше он совершенно не знал. Другого учителя зловерия, на большее прельщение человеческого рода, злокозненный диавол представил ему в лице некоего инока, выгнанного из Константинополя за арианскую ересь и другие богомерзкие его хулы.
own_translation_en: Everything of this he was taught by a Jew, of which he had known nothing before. The devil, to lead the human race into a greater delusion, presented to him another teacher of error in the person of a certain monk, expelled from Constantinople for the Arian heresy and for his other abominable blasphemies.
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
licence_note: azbyka.ru 1910 printing, team to confirm public domain status.
keys: выгнанного из Константинополя за арианскую ересь
what_it_says: Muhammad's teaching came from a Jewish teacher and an Arian monk, according to a polemical legend; Maxim calls it a deception.
context: Part of Maxim's account of how Muhammad came to his teaching: first a Jew teaches him circumcision, abstention from pork, ritual washing and the permission of many wives, then an Arian monk takes over. Maxim presents it as a legend reported by 'writers who know this reliably', not as verified history.
limits: Legendary narrative, not history. Maxim cites no named source ('as the writers who know this reliably have passed on'). Passage contains the epithet 'скверный' and 'инок' polemic against a monk. The legend is a Byzantine motif; source not identified in this session. Famous status: UNVERIFIED.
stance: reporting (repeats a polemical legend, then refutes it)
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
cross_check: k-istine.ru: present (key phrases match after whitespace normalisation). paraklit.org: 'выгнанного из Константинополя за арианскую ересь' present. Status: VERIFIED in 3 copies, with minor wording variants in the first key.

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): о Коране и Евангелии
quote_orig: Хотя во многих местах проклятой его книги, называемой «Коран» на словах и превозносит божественное и священное Евангелие Христа Спасителя, называя его справедливым и правильным, но на деле совсем не то: ибо скверный сей всюду вводит законы, противные ему.
own_translation_en: Although in many places of his cursed book, which they call 'the Qur'an', he verbally extols the divine and holy Gospel of Christ the Saviour, calling it just and right, in fact it is quite otherwise: for this wicked man everywhere introduces laws contrary to it.
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
keys: Хотя во многих местах проклятой его книги
ибо скверный сей всюду вводит законы, противные ему
what_it_says: The Qur'an praises the Gospel only in words, while its laws contradict it, according to Maxim.
context: Maxim is answering a claim that the Qur'an accepts the Gospel. He argues that the praise is verbal only and that the Qur'an's laws contradict the Gospel. This sets up his later argument from John 1 and from the Gospel commands.
limits: The quoted text is Maxim's paraphrase of the Qur'an's stance, not a Qur'anic quotation. He does not give a Qur'an reference here. The contradiction claim is UNVERIFIED against the Qur'an in this session. Passage uses 'скверный' (wicked) for Muhammad.
stance: own view (quoting the Qur'an's position as Maxim presents it)
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
cross_check: Present in all three copies; the second sentence differs only in capitalisation ('Ибо' in k-istine.ru and paraklit.org vs 'ибо' in azbyka.ru). Status: VERIFIED in 3 copies (text, case variants).

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): о Божестве Христа по Ин. 1:1–3, 14
quote_orig: Благовременно может кто-либо, обращаясь к нему, сказать: «Если ты считаешь божественное и поклоняемое Христово Евангелие сшедшим с неба, и потому называешь и признаешь его справедливым и правильным, то зачем противиться ему, когда оно так ясно свидетельствует о Божестве Христовом, говоря:  «В начале бе Слово, и Слово бе к Богу, и Бог бе Слово, Сей бе искони к Богу» (Иоан. 1, 1–2). Слышишь ли, что  Тот, Который был в начале к Богу – Слово, есть Бог, как и рождающий Его Бог-Отец? Ты же, о нечестивейший, зачем отметаешь Божество Его и называешь Его только святым человеком, лишь высшим прочих пророков?
own_translation_en: It is well-timed for someone, addressing him, to say: 'If you consider the divine and worshipped Gospel of Christ to have come down from heaven, and therefore call and acknowledge it as just and right, why do you oppose it, when it so clearly testifies to the divinity of Christ, saying, 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God' (John 1:1–2)? ... You, most impious one, why do you reject his divinity and call him only a holy man, only higher than the other prophets?'
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
keys: называешь Его только святым человеком, лишь высшим прочих пророков
what_it_says: Maxim argues from John 1 that Christ is God the Word, and so the Qur'anic view of Christ as only a prophet is false.
context: Maxim addresses Muhammad in the second person, as a rhetorical device. The argument is built on John 1:1–3, 14 and on the voice from heaven at the Transfiguration (Matt. 17:5). It is a direct doctrinal reply to the Islamic view of Christ as a prophet and not God.
limits: Rhetorical second-person address to Muhammad; the view attributed is Maxim's summary of the Muslim position. The rejection of Christ's divinity is attributed to the Qur'an only as Maxim presents it. The passage is long (98 words) and includes ellipses (…) in my own translation, which mark omitted Scripture citations. Famous status: UNVERIFIED.
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
cross_check: k-istine.ru and paraklit.org: both key phrases present (verbatim after whitespace normalisation). Status: VERIFIED in 3 copies.

ref: «Ответы христиан против агарян (мусульман)» (Догматико-полемические сочинения, гл. 8 по paraklit.org): начало текста
quote_orig: Если же хотите заградить им уста и посрамить их, то не приводите им доказательств ни из какого другого боговдохновеннаго писания, как только из Евангелия, ибо бесовдохновенная их книга, называемая у них «Коран», во многих местах хвалит святое Евангелие, и называет его правильным и святым и считает ниспосланным с неба.
own_translation_en: If you want to stop their mouths and put them to shame, do not bring them proofs from any other God-inspired scripture, but only from the Gospel, for their demon-inspired book, called by them 'the Qur'an', in many places praises the holy Gospel, and calls it right and holy, and considers it sent down from heaven.
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
licence_note: paraklit.org: no licence statement seen; a devotional reproduction site. The underlying 1910 text is public domain; team to confirm the site's edition.
keys: бесовдохновенная их книга, называемая у них «Коран»
во многих местах хвалит святое Евангелие
what_it_says: In his answers to Muslims, Maxim advises using the Gospel alone as proof, because the Qur'an itself praises it.
context: From Maxim's practical guide 'Answers of Christians to the Hagarenes', which teaches Christians how to argue with Muslims. He recommends using the Qur'an's own praise of the Gospel as the common ground.
limits: Paraklit.org text, which gives no edition or year. The 'demon-inspired' epithet is polemical. The claim that the Qur'an calls the Gospel 'sent down from heaven' is Maxim's statement; not checked against the Qur'an in this session. Famous status: UNVERIFIED. Single witness (paraklit.org).
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
cross_check: Only paraklit.org read for this passage (single witness). The azbyka.ru 'Ответы' page was not opened. Status: UNVERIFIED beyond one copy.

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): ответ «Магомета» на требование знамения
quote_orig: Он же грубо и гордо ответил на это, говоря: «Моисей и бывшие после него, так называемые, пророки и сам Христос были посланы от Бога с чудесами и различными знамениями, а я послан с мечом и имею повеление убивать непокоряющихся моим словам».
own_translation_en: Then he answered rudely and proudly, saying: 'Moses and those after him, the so-called prophets, and Christ himself were sent by God with miracles and various signs; but I was sent with the sword and have the command to kill those who do not obey my words.'
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
keys: имею повеление убивать непокоряющихся моим словам
what_it_says: Muhammad is said to reply to a demand for a sign that he was sent with the sword; Maxim says God compels no one, so he is not from God.
context: This is Maxim's account of a dialogue: Arabs ask Muhammad for a sign, as they had asked of Moses and Christ, and he answers with the sword. Maxim uses the reply to argue that Muhammad is not sent by God, because God compels no one (the next sentences).
limits: FLAGGED FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR. The quoted claim is a call to kill (Muhammad's claimed command), which the exclusion rule (rule 3) excludes as an insult/war call. The point of the passage is Maxim's doctrinal refutation (God does not compel; no miracles), so I have kept it under theme S (arms). Drop it if the team reads the rule strictly. The dialogue is Maxim's narrative, with no other source named. Famous status: UNVERIFIED. CROSS-CHECK: this passage is absent from paraklit.org and k-istine.ru; only the azbyka.ru text has it.
stance: quoting opponent (Maxim quotes Muhammad's claim, then refutes it)

Check the Kazan 1859 edition before use.

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): описание рая после рассказа о голубе
quote_orig: Имея в себе всецело живущим самого диавола, который и говорил чрез него то, что служит к вечной погибели слушающих, он дозволил им всякое вообще наслаждение и все то, что может услаждать гортань, чрево и подчревное, говоря, что на то мы и сначала были созданы от общего всех Создателя, и что поэтому в созданном им раю Создатель приготовил для них, по словам скверного сего, три реки, состояния из меду, вина и молока, и отроковиц множество прекрасных, с которыми они будут весь день совокупляться и которые на другой день опять оказываются девами.
own_translation_en: Having in himself the devil himself living wholly within him, who spoke through him what serves to the eternal perdition of those who listen, he allowed them every kind of pleasure and everything that can gratify the palate, the belly and what lies below; saying that for that very reason we were created in the beginning by the common Creator of all, and that therefore in the paradise He made, the Creator has prepared for them, according to this wicked man's words, three rivers, of honey, wine and milk, and a multitude of beautiful maidens with whom they will be joined all day, and who on the next day again prove to be virgins.
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
keys: три реки, состояния из меду, вина и молока
с которыми они будут весь день совокупляться
what_it_says: The paradise promised by Muhammad is one of carnal pleasures, which Maxim presents as the lure that won followers.
context: Maxim's description of the paradise promised by Muhammad (carnal promises), given as the lure that won followers. It comes after the account of Muhammad's wife and the claimed angelic visits, and before the pigeon episode.
limits: Maxim's description of Qur'anic paradise is not checked against the Qur'an text in this session. The sexual content is quoted only as Maxim's words. The phrase 'the devil himself living within him' is polemical language. Famous status: UNVERIFIED.

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): о клятвах для обмана христиан
quote_orig: К тому же, если Божественное Евангелие справедливо и правильно, как сам говоришь, и как мы веруем и исповедуем, то зачем, вопреки заповеданию Евангелия отнюдь не клясться ни небом, ни землею, и ни чем иным, ты, нечестивейший, повелеваешь своим последователям не отказываться ни от какого вида клятвы для обмана христиан?
own_translation_en: Moreover, if the divine Gospel is just and right, as you yourself say, and as we believe and confess, why, contrary to the Gospel's commandment to swear absolutely not at all, neither by heaven nor by earth nor by anything else, do you, most impious one, command your followers not to refuse any form of oath in order to deceive Christians?
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
keys: повелеваешь своим последователям не отказываться ни от какого вида клятвы для обмана христиан
what_it_says: Maxim accuses Muhammad of ordering oaths to deceive Christians, contrary to the Gospel's ban on oaths (UNVERIFIED against the Qur'an).
context: Maxim's charge that the Qur'an, which claims to respect the Gospel, instructs Muslims to swear oaths in order to deceive Christians. He reads the instruction as a plan to destroy Christian rulers.
limits: This is a charge of doctrinal deceit against Muhammad. Maxim does not give a Qur'anic reference, and I did NOT verify the instruction against the Qur'an. The charge is UNVERIFIED. Note: it is a sharp accusation about the faithful's practice; the team should check the Qur'anic basis before presenting it.
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)

ref: Слово 1 (гл. 6 по paraklit.org; «Два слова», 1910): ответ на обвинение христиан в искажении Писания
quote_orig: Но, быть может, по премногому твоему безстыдству и беснованию, ты дерзнешь клеветать на христиан, говоря, что они сами написали это о Христе в Евангелии? Пусть будет и так, как ты, клевеща на нас, говоришь. Неужели же и те пророческие книги, которые имеются у евреев, и которые ясно проповедуют Христа Богом, Сыном Божиим и Творцем всего, мы испортили?
own_translation_en: But perhaps, through your great shamelessness and frenzy, you will dare to slander Christians, saying that they themselves wrote this about Christ in the Gospel? Let it be so, as you say, slandering us. Have we then corrupted also the prophetic books which the Jews have, which clearly proclaim Christ as God, the Son of God and Creator of all?
quote_latin: none (Russian text only; no Latin printed)
what_it_says: Maxim turns back the charge that Christians corrupted the Gospel, asking if they also corrupted the Jewish prophets, who proclaim Christ as God.
context: Maxim answers the Muslim charge (in his presentation) that Christians wrote the Gospel's teaching about Christ's divinity. He turns it back by asking whether Christians also corrupted the Jewish prophetic books, which he says proclaim Christ as God.
limits: The 'Muslim charge' of corruption is Maxim's reconstruction in the second person; he does not quote the Qur'an here. It is an argument, not a Qur'anic text. Famous status: UNVERIFIED. The Russian is a 1910 translation.
stance: own view (reply to an opponent's charge)
famous_where: UNVERIFIED: not found cited in the sources I opened (answering-islam.org Byzantine survey: 0 mentions of Maxim; en.wikipedia: no Islam mention)
